memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "At that time, Judah left his brothers and went down to stay with a man of Adullam named Hirah." - Gen 38:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This chapter opens with Judah stepping away from his family: "Judah left his brothers and went down." The word "down" is telling. Judah separates himself from the covenant family and goes to live among the Canaanites, striking up a friendship with a local man. It is a small move on the surface, but it marks the beginning of a spiritual drift — and as the chapter unfolds, that drift leads Judah into moral ruin.

Notice the timing, too. This happens right after Judah had helped sell his own brother Joseph into slavery (Gen 37:26-27). Perhaps his conscience was uneasy; perhaps he simply wanted distance. Whatever the reason, when we carry unconfessed sin, we often start to drift — away from those who know us, away from accountability, away from God.

Drifting rarely happens all at once. It begins with a single step "down" and away, a quiet loosening of the ties that once held us close to God and His people. One step leads to another, and before long we find ourselves somewhere we never intended to be.

Guard against the drift. Stay close to God's people, keep your heart open and accountable, and deal honestly with the sin that tempts you to isolate. "Let us not give up meeting together" (Heb 10:25), for it is often when we wander off alone that we wander into trouble.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I drifting away from God's people or from accountability?
2. Is there unconfessed sin making me want to isolate?
3. What one step could I take to stay close rather than drift?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from drifting away from You and Your people. Where sin makes me want to isolate, draw me back into honesty and fellowship. Hold me close to You. Amen.
